text:
perf-bot: CI PERF ALERT — staging throughput drop ~18% on branch 'main' after merge rfc/model-bump-3.2.1 (CI job: perf/staging/throughput).

jack: saw the alert, rolling it up. last successful commit before regression: 0a1b2c3 (model-onboard/v3.2.0). suspect the model bump.

ella: concrete numbers from the last run: median latency +60ms, p95 +120ms, tokens/sec -18%.

sanjay: correlates with scheduler choosing the generic matmul kernel more often. profiler snapshot: 
```
kernel_selector: chosen_kernel=matmul_generic
fallback_reason=tokenizer_seq_len>128
batcher: avg_seq=82 -> now avg_seq=110
kv_cache: hit_rate=0.85 (baseline 0.98)
```

mia: wait — why did avg_seq jump? the model checkpoint change included a tokenizer patch (unicode normalizer tweak) that seems to keep leading spaces. That inflates token counts on many prompts.

jack: so tokenizer change -> longer sequences -> batcher heuristic flips -> different kernel chosen -> higher exec cost. plus kv cache eviction churn from slightly different key prefixes -> lower cache hit rate. compounded.

ella: timeline: PR #4321 (model bump + tokenizer tweak) merged Tue 08:14. First perf regression in nightly Wed 02:00. Bisect plan?

sanjay: quick bisect script to narrow to tokenizer vs model weights: run this locally against the perf harness:
```
# reproduce perf job locally
./tools/perf/run_harness --model=main --checkpoint=HEAD~1 --tokens=10000 --trace=profile.json
# compare with HEAD
./tools/perf/run_harness --model=main --checkpoint=HEAD --tokens=10000 --trace=profile2.json
```

mia: I ran that against the checkpoint only (weights but old tokenizer) — perf matched baseline. When I run with the new tokenizer + old weights, the avg_seq jumps to 107 and kernel selector flips.

jack: OK that's pretty conclusive. Tokenizer change is primary. What about KV cache hit drop?

sanjay: KV cache keying uses token ids + model_id + tokenizer_normalizer_hash. The normalizer tweak changed casing/whitespace behavior so previously identical prefixes are now tokenized differently — cache no longer matches. We should have flagged tokenizer-normalizer_hash in the onboard checklist.

ella: mitigation options: 1) revert tokenizer tweak in production, 2) update cache keying to ignore the normalizer variant (hard), 3) teach kernel selector to be robust to modest seq-length shifts (short term).

jack: immediate action: block rollout, revert tokenizer change from PR #4321 for hosted canary. Can someone file rollback and a canary hold?

ops-bot: rollout: blocked for release/redwood-hosted/canary — reason: perf regression detected by perf-bot.

mia: filing rollback PR now -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4352 (revert tokenizer normalizer tweak).

perf-bot: re-running perf job on canary after revert...

sanjay: while we wait, we should add an invariant test to CI: compare avg tokenization length distribution between tokenizers (baseline vs candidate) and fail if >10% shift. small test patch incoming.

ella: also adding a test for kv cache key stability: ensure tokenizer-normalizer-hash is present in onboarding checklist and warns on change.

perf-bot: CI: perf/staging/throughput (after revert) — green. metrics: median latency back within 3% of baseline, tokens/sec +-1.

jack: great. we'll merge the revert PR to canary and then to main after a short soak. Follow-ups:
- sanitize tokenizer onboarding docs
- add CI tokenization distribution check
- revisit kernel selector thresholds to avoid flip on ~20% seq changes
- investigate KV cache key layering to be tolerant of normalizer metadata changes

mia: noted and added follow-up issues: #781 (tokenizer checklist), #782 (ci tokenization distribution test), #783 (kernel-selector threshold), #784 (kv-cache keying).

jack: thanks all. summary for release notes: 'blocked model bump due to tokenizer normalization change causing elevated latency and reduced KV cache hit rate; reverted tokenizer patch and added CI guardrails.' :thumbsup:
